step_findings.detail: For any selected index set, cutting the word changes its product from UV to VU = U^{-1}(UV)U. Thus identity and cardinality are preserved in both directions. Undoing the cut and sorting the selected original indices gives the required original-order subword. Pairs crossing the original boundary cause no problem. Cutting immediately after a reflection leaves every cyclic rotation gap intact.

Starting with u_1=0, reflection-selection bits uniquely reconstruct u_{t+1}=u_t XOR [f_t selected]. Pair-selection bits then uniquely reconstruct every m_pi. Fixing u_1 removes the global-complement ambiguity. An empty selection forces all u_t=0 and then all m_pi=0; conversely, zero parameters select nothing.

A closed binary cycle has an even number of transitions, and each selected pair contributes two letters. Hence the size is even and at most N<=4p-1. For F=1 the construction remains defined, but the hypothesis is impossible: F+floor((N-1)/2)<=2p<3p-1.

Before any letter in X_t or the reflection f_t, the selected-reflection count is sum_{s<t}[u_s!=u_{s+1}], whose parity telescopes to u_t because u_1=0. Thus its coordinate contribution has sign c_t=(-1)^{u_t}. The total reflection count is even because u_{F+1}=u_1, so the final second coordinate is +1.

For Boolean colours, [u_t!=u_{t+1}]c_t=u_{t+1}-u_t. Summation by parts gives sum_t (u_{t+1}-u_t)y_t=sum_{t=2}^F u_t(y_{t-1}-y_t), with both boundary terms zero. The pair identity is valid: when u=0 it equals xm; when u=1 it equals -x(1-m)=xm-x. Collecting terms gives precisely the stated beta_t and V. Singletons contribute nothing.

The integer XOR expressions give Z=|S| on the Boolean box and degree at most two. V has degree at most one. Therefore deg Q<=3(p-1)=3p-3, while M=F+sum floor(n_t/2)-1>=3p-2. The required inequality is strict, including at the hypothesis boundary.

Every monomial of total degree below M omits a variable; flipping that coordinate cancels its signed sum. Fermat's theorem makes Q exactly the indicator of V=Z=0 over F_p on the box. Here |x| denotes parameter Hamming weight, distinct from selection size. The zero parameter point contributes 1, so it cannot be the only solution when the signed sum is zero.

The nonzero solution selects a nonempty set. Its size is even, divisible by the odd prime p, and below 4p. Consequently its size is exactly 2p. The coordinate calculation and even reflection parity give the identity product, including after restoring original order.

Exactly 3p-1 reflections satisfy the theorem with every gap empty. Any longer word containing at least 3p-1 reflections also inherits the conclusion by first taking that many reflections in original order. The proof does not establish the full dihedral ordered Olson statement.

counterexample_attempts: No counterexample found. Independent bitmask dynamic programming, tracking ordered subsequence products directly, exhaustively excluded every qualifying p=3 word through length 11 using 16,670 compressed states. For p=5, exhaustive searches covered ten representative two/three-letter alphabets through length 19 and all reflection-only words at length 14. Additional independent tests checked 194,138 p=5 words: two random residue assignments for each of all 97,069 qualifying type patterns, including cyclic cuts. Arbitrary-residue mixed p=5 words were sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Negative controls found reflection-only avoiders at length 3p-2 for both primes. The supplied scripts also passed, including complete parameter enumeration for 410 qualifying p=3 samples and 94 qualifying p=5 samples.
novelty_or_prior_art_notes: I do not know prior literature proving this exact Theorem P or the full dihedral ordered Olson statement. No external literature was consulted under the read restriction. This verdict establishes proof validity, not novelty. The Boolean-box cancellation argument is elementary and sufficient without invoking any stronger mixed-modulus theorem.
